name: Rust Brown
lede: Rust brown is a reddish brown named for the corrosion on iron, and the books treat it as a plain descriptive name.

sections.title: A reddish brown
sections.body:
Paterson defines rust brown as reddish-brown, the same gloss it gives plain rust [1]. In its index rust brown sits in the brown group beside russet, rusty and Sahara [1]. Paterson also defines [[russet]] as a reddish brown, though it traces that word to a coarse cloth [1].

One chemistry passage uses the phrase literally: the Pigment Compendium says vanadium(V) oxide forms crystals that range from yellow to rust brown [2]. That is a description of a look, not a pigment [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The library value is a deep reddish brown, a screen approximation [3]. In our archive 385 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.6%, carry a close match covering at least 5% of the canvas [4]. The earliest is *Hunt of the Hare*, about 1150, where it covers about 57% [4]. Titian's *Cardinal Pietro Bembo* of 1539 covers about 34% [4].

origin.source: Paterson, A Dictionary of Colour, p. 350
